problem: Matched to the modern Republic of Armenia (Q399) with countries [Armenia]. Several region texts mean historical Armenia: 'Armenia (Ani, Vaspurakan)' names Ani and Vaspurakan, which lie in eastern Turkey today (Ani in Kars province, Vaspurakan around Lake Van), and 'Armenia, Byzantium' means the medieval Armenian lands. A reader would be told these places are in today's Armenia, which is wrong. (Locations of Ani and Vaspurakan rest on my own knowledge, not the data given.)
suggestion: Match the historical region of Armenia (Armenian Highlands / historical Armenia) rather than the modern state, at least for the 'Ani, Vaspurakan' and 'Byzantium' entries. Country set: Armenia, Turkey at minimum; historical Armenia also reaches into Iran and Azerbaijan, so the builder should check that item's P17.

problem: The region text is 'Aksum (Ethiopia/Eritrea)', which is the Aksumite kingdom. The item is the town of Axum (Q5832), so the countries are [Ethiopia] only. The basis says openly that the item is the town, but the entry's own text names Eritrea, and the kingdom covered much of present-day Eritrea.
suggestion: Match the Kingdom of Aksum, or keep the town as a stated proxy, but set countries to Ethiopia, Eritrea as the region text says.

problem: The region text says 'Caucasian Albania (modern Azerbaijan/Dagestan)', but the countries are only [Azerbaijan]. Dagestan is a republic of Russia, so the text itself names a second present-day country.
suggestion: Countries: Azerbaijan, Russia. Some reconstructions also put a small part in eastern Georgia; the builder could check the item's P17 or its description for that. (The Georgia point rests on my own knowledge.)

problem: Matched to the modern state of Syria (Q858). Most of the region texts mean Roman or late-antique Syria: 'Palestine, Syria', 'Asia Minor, Syria, Egypt, Rome...', 'Syria, Mesopotamia'. That historical Syria included Antioch, which is in Turkey's Hatay province today, and the Lebanese coast. One country fits the Telanissos and Laodicea entries, but it understates the region the other entries mean. (Based on my own knowledge of the Roman province's extent.)
suggestion: Think about using a historical-region item (Roman Syria / the Levant) with countries Syria, Turkey, Lebanon for the late-antique entries. Or keep the modern state as a stated proxy and accept it.

problem: Matched to the modern Free State of Saxony (Q1202). For 'Gandersheim Abbey, Saxony (Ottonian Germany)' that is the wrong Saxony. Ottonian Saxony was the old Duchy of Saxony, and Gandersheim lies in today's Lower Saxony, not in the Free State of Saxony. The Reformation-era entries ('Saxony, then N. Europe') mean the Electorate, which only partly matches the modern state. The country, Germany, is right in every case. (Based on my own knowledge.)
suggestion: Keep Germany. For the Gandersheim entry, think about matching the Duchy of Saxony or Lower Saxony instead of the Free State.

problem: The countries are [Poland, Germany, Czech Republic], from P17. The item's own description reads 'historical region in Germany and Poland'. Whether any of historical Upper Lusatia lies in the Czech Republic today depends on the definition used, so the Czech Republic may mislead.
suggestion: Check this. If the historical margraviate's bounds are meant, Germany, Poland is probably the correct set (my own knowledge, not certain).

problem: The Ethiopian Highlands extend north into the Eritrean highlands, but the countries are [Ethiopia] only. The region text gives no further context. (Based on my own knowledge of the range's extent.)
suggestion: Think about Ethiopia, Eritrea, if the entry means the highland Christian heartland as a whole (for example the Aksumite and Tigrinya-speaking north).

problem: The proxy is broader than the place: the item is the whole Ethiopian Highlands, and the text means only the northern part, around Lake Tana. The basis says so openly. Ethiopia alone is probably right, since the text pairs it with Lake Tana, but 'northern highlands' could also take in the Eritrean plateau.
suggestion: Keep Ethiopia unless the entry's source means to include the Eritrean plateau.

problem: The proxy is much broader than the place: the item is all of Asia Minor (Q12824780) for the Roman province of Bithynia and Pontus. The country, Turkey, is correct. A narrower item already in this set is Bithynia (Q373189), and the province itself probably has its own item.
suggestion: Match the Roman province of Bithynia and Pontus, or Bithynia, instead of Asia Minor. Countries stay Turkey.

problem: The proxy is broader than the place: the item is the whole island of Great Britain for 'western Britain' (in the text 'Wales, W. Britain, Cornwall, Brittany'). The country, United Kingdom, is correct.
suggestion: This is acceptable as a stated proxy. No change to the countries.
